name: HottyScrollView: a log and a document
description: A box of a fixed height whose content scrolls, as bubbles' viewport. The log is lines bound to /log, as an agent adds them (an index each; the data model has no append), and follows its tail: it starts at the end. Its long lines are cut, and ← and → scroll them. The document is a Text child. Tab into either. In cells, bubbles' keys scroll it: the arrows, j and k, Page Up and Page Down (b, f, Space), u and d, Home and End (g, G), and the wheel. On a HOTTY host the host scrolls it, with the keys a browser scrolls with, the wheel, and the same letters, which the box binds to the host's scroll actions (SPEC §10.2); a host older than those scrolls with the arrows, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End only.

components.text:
## Scrolling in a terminal

A terminal app shows more than fits by scrolling a part of the screen, not the whole of it. A **pager** shows a document a screen at a time; a **log** keeps its newest lines in view as they arrive.

### The keys

- ↑ and ↓, or k and j, move a line.
- Page Up and Page Down, or b and f, move a page; Space moves a page down.
- u and d move half a page.
- Home and End, or g and G, go to the ends.

### Following the tail

A log that follows its tail starts at the end and stays there as lines come. Scroll up to read, and it stays where you are; scroll back down, and it follows again.

### On a HOTTY host

There the host scrolls the box itself, with its own scrollbar, the wheel, the touchpad and the keys a browser scrolls with, as a page scrolls in a browser. The letters above work there too: the box hands them to the host's scrolling.

### In cells

Here the kit draws the box and its scrollbar: a track down its right edge, and a thumb as long as the share of the content that shows.
